keyVerseText: For an angel went down at a certain season into the pool, and troubled the water: whosoever then first after the troubling of the water stepped in was made whole of whatsoever disease he had.
rootMeaning: The word δήποτε (dḗpote) combines the particles δή and ποτέ, where δή emphasizes certainty or explicitness, and ποτέ relates to time, meaning 'at some time' or 'ever.' Together, δήποτε conveys a sense of indefiniteness with an element of emphasis, often rendered as 'whatsoever' or 'at any time.' This root sense adds a nuance beyond a simple English gloss by highlighting both the generalizing and emphatic nature of the term, suggesting not just any time but with a certain assuredness or definiteness.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, δήποτε appears only once, translated as 'whatsoever,' indicating a particle of generalization that can be absolute or combined with other words to express indefiniteness or inclusiveness. Its singular occurrence in John 5:4 shows it functioning to emphasize the comprehensive scope of healing, applying to any disease without limitation. This usage reveals that the term serves to underscore the all-encompassing nature of the statement it accompanies.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding δήποτε enriches our grasp of God's boundless power and mercy as portrayed in Scripture. The particle's emphatic generalization reminds believers that God's healing and grace are not restricted by time, condition, or circumstance but are available 'whatsoever' the need may be. This aligns with the evangelical conviction of Christ's sufficiency for all sins and infirmities, reinforcing trust in His comprehensive care. The word's original meaning invites believers to embrace the fullness of God's provision without reservation, confident in His sovereign ability to act at any time and in any situation.
keyVerseReflection: John 5:4 speaks of an angel troubling the waters of a pool so that 'whosoever then first after the troubling of the water stepped in was made whole of whatsoever disease he had.' Here, δήποτε emphasizes the unlimited scope of healing available—any disease without exception. The word strengthens the verse's assurance that God's healing power is not selective but extends to every possible ailment, inviting faith in divine restoration regardless of the specific condition.
